Good game but.. 1. Unfinished game. This is only act 1, it is early access. Unfinished games should be marked early access, this is just avoiding filters to trick people. 2. The game doesnt make clear that you have to limit it down to one tile before being able to find the target. I spent a bit too much time running around to see if i could find the target early just to find out it wasnt possible, the target isnt actually in the forest until you find them.. This means instead of actually looking for a target and narrowing down the area to do so, you are just running from dealer to card usage spot back to dealer back to.... It rewards being good with the cards sure, but that just changes how often you do that repetitive run.

I like the story and characters, but the gameplay is incredibly tedious. I am tired of uninspired indie horror games where you walk, get jumpscared and that is it. The devs clearly tried their best to do something different, but went about it the wrong way. Instead of walking around, we are running around the entire time trying to avoid monsters. That just teleport anyway. What is the point of portals if they don't help me get away from the monsters? Not to mention how often they appear on top of you when you come out of the card world. Honestly, I think the game would have been better if they went for something without player movement or free-roaming. Something that wasn't just walking and walking and walking, and that took much less time so I could get back to the story quicker. But who cares about my opinion? It has a lot of thumbnail-worthy monsters and all the streamers will be screeching at the jumpscare animations, so its going to blow up anyway.

Some of the mosters, especially [spoiler] the Little Rabbit [/spoiler] was SUPER stressful and freaky! Overall a really positive experience! I CAN'T WAIT for Act 2 and 3!!

[h2]Eating the Rich and Losing Weight Doing it![/h2] We've all wanted to snack on a millionaire, billionaire and now... if we play our cards right: A Trillionaire! And this game gives us the chance to do what it takes to make the world a better place. [b]STORY[/b] Can't spoil a thing. But I will say if you expect a generic horror story, you'll quickly see how quick this toothy hole goes. Nothing is slapped into your face, there are subtle things and good reasons to replay (clues I missed the first time!) [b] GAMEPLAY [/b] It's a bit clunky at times but I'm a bit old and have essential tremors so it might be smoother than I think. Could do with some gentle tuning but I'm liking what I'm seeing so far (Beware: Fall Damage ahead!) It was actually nice that I could be in the water... I'm so used to being kept out of it that it shocked me when I waded right through instead of dying! [b]GRAPHICS[/b] You're not going to be wow'd with top of the line realism and crazy indepth graphical detail. But I love the character design, the overall world is crafted and not just slapped together. [b]OVERALL[/b] Fantastic game so far. Worth the price even not on discount. There's amazing little jokes, nods to other games/genres and little easter eggs. Can't wait for more!

ABSOLUTE PEAK, would FEED THE PIT again the game feels like a really cool blend of squirrel stapler with the map designes, and a mix of battleship & hide and seek in terms of the hunt itself. Monsters that hunt you are also really well done, simple enough to be understandable but not so simple as to know how they work right off the start, even now i'm sure i missed some of their mechanics/attacks. story wise, the characters are suprsingly wholesome, and the overall plot complex enough to make you think about how it will be continues for quite a bit after you finish the game. the only thing i can say in terms of negatives for now is that i don't see much replayability unless you want 100% attachments, but that's only cos the future acts arent out yet, i'm sure the devs will add higher difficulties levels and eventually a custome game mode once they finish up the story. even so, 100% worth the price, the 4-5h i got out of it so far and the promise of more to come got me super hyped for the future acts and updates.

Clarification/ tl;dr. My main point is that if this game (which is not labeled early access) and it's single, 3 hour long act 1 doesn't feel worth the ten dollars, then I'd just wishlist/follow the game for when the rest of the game is released, and then play it. I'm expecting I'll be able to get 12-16 hours out of this game when it's ACTUALLY done and not a 10 dollar demo. If you want to buy the game now, experience what it currently has, and are willing to then play it again as new acts release, then that's fine! But I felt a little cheated at how short act 1 felt and how unpolished the enemy design felt. Those flaming me in the comments are all valid, because they believe it's worth it. Hell, I liked the game. But this is about recommending the game to others like friends and strangers alike; and with that, it's really hard recommend as the game as is right now. ========================= Great game! Great story, scary gameplay, awesome vibes, amazing concept. I've been waiting for this game for a good while now. However, as much as I love it, I struggle to recommend it in its current state. For a game that's 10 dollars, it's really a glorified demo. Only 3 hours of content, for a VERY linear story, with no replayability whatsoever beyond a hard mode which I doubt most will be interested in tackling after having played the normal mode. The worst part is; if this game was labeled Early Access, I'd have recommended it. But I know why they avoided the Early Access tag; it's a detriment to getting sales. There is a substantial subset of players that will avoid Early Access games, and for good reason. It feels scummy for a game that provides so little for 10 dollars to not be labeled as Early Access just to get a bunch of early sales. It rubs me the wrong way. That said, if they're not going to label it as Early Access, I need to review the game as it is. A 3 hour, 10 dollar game, with a demo-esque ending that made me feel like any other demo I've played.

Hunt down a target into a shifting forest, while avoiding the local cryptids. Feed The Pit is a really good experience. I only got into it because I loved their previous game, The Deadseat, and because I thought the gameplay looked novel. I'm glad I did because I ended up getting absorbed in the game's story. The basic gameplay loop is a game of battleship, except you're hunting for one person and you use differing cards to narrow down where they are. Each card used rules out more land, as you slowly narrow down their location. Meanwhile the local... wildlife needs to avoided. It seems you're not the most dangerous thing in this forest. I love the feel of locating your target: you need one last check to find where they're hiding. Listening for the heartbeat getting louder, tracking their footprints. Like a frightened deer they bolt, smashing past you. It takes a moment to recover yourself, yours eyes firmly set on your prey. You dash after them, your prey outlined in a big red glow. They're fast, but after a distance they slow down. You don't. Your endurance is otherwordly. When you finally catch them, it's an undignified struggle. You fall on top of each other, and you frantically stab and stab over and over until they stop moving. A moment passes. They're dead. You've done it. The trek back to the van is in contemplative silence. The hardest part is over, and all that's left is your thoughts. Despite how much I love the gameplay here, it's so much more. I love the characters in this: each one has their own unique model and mannerisms. The blind Father has difficulty using objects, the handless Protector fidgets with his prosthetic nervously as he talks. For a story about feeding people to a flesh pit, it drew me in. There's something more. Something even stranger, as unbelieveable as it sounds. There's even bits completely outside the normal gameplay: segments resembling old school rpgs or text based adventures. I'm getting vibes of Inscryption, and I'm tentatively hoping they can deliver on that. If I had one criticism, it'd be that we should be able to replay previous hunts for the sake of achievments. But hey it's early days yet. It took me 3 hours to beat Act one. If the other two acts are of similar length/quality, I'd say its well worth the money. Good luck! And remember. The Breach is coming.

SPOILER WARNING(I tried to be light on spoilers in case your eyes accidentally read it, so js try to skip past if you haven't played it yet) I apologize in advance if I sound like im rambling or have some bad takes, I never have written a review like this before, but this game deserved it. Please take it with a grain of salt. Genuinely one of my top games I've played this year. For something only having 1 act released so far, I've gotten more lore and theories than I could've asked for. The characters have such loveable personalities(except the medium, ♥♥♥♥ you for not liking acolyte's lemon bars) and are far more discernable than just special members of the cult. The cardmaster is also a nice difference compared to true assistants in how he actually doesn't agree with the church, but still listens to the cards(also rosemary is the goat) But the real treat to this game is the gameplay. For something as simple as closing in on a square with nothing but some cards, there is not a lot you would expect from it, yet Feed The Pit takes it and makes it one of the most enjoyable experiences ever. The unique items you can also collect are very useful(#icarusfeather) but also don't feel so overpowered that you need it to complete your mission. The balance is done well to where the items serve more as a quality of life than an absolute necessity to win. Worldbuilding might also be one of the biggest wins in this game(Shoutout Birb Gaming for my new favorite phrase from this game: "I LOVE BLUE WORLD!"). Carrister Valley is incredibly well designed with the forest changing to suit your new targets, but also not being overbearing to make it hard to find them. The church itself hits a home run on the cult feeling with the closet of belongings of the members of the church along with everything else. Then there's the pit itself, and damn that scared me the first time since I didn't see a single review or trailer before buying the game. The pit's clashing ideals with the Father also make for an interesting plot with how the father may be going crazy or warping the pit's wishes into his own. The backstory and mini games also are great, but that mini game walking through the forest-- Yeah I'm paranoid now. The backstory with the members is quite well developed for how short you actually see them, and this branched a ton of theories between me and my friend group. This game has so many positives that I could keep going. But I do have a few issues with the game that should be addressed, which are minor except for my first one: Balance of enemies. Correct me if I am wrong(I tend to be heavily ignorant at times), but enemy difficulty should increase the further in you go, and it feels more like a roller coaster than a linear line. First is the Spriggan, which is actually fairly difficult since you need to keep your head on a swivel for the whole mission to stay alive, but other than that it's not too bad. Then you reach the bunny girl, which is by far the easiest enemy in the game. I do think it could be cool if they brought her back with a much more difficult childhood game to play, but it's merely a suggestion. Then, you reach the flesh demon, and dear god that guy scared the sh*t out of me. He isn't as hard as the Spriggan, since you can js run to a portal and be fine for a bit, but jesus christ that first time he sprinted at me I nearly closed the game. Only thing I wished for from here is making enemy difficulty increase instead of it going hardest, then easiest, then pretty damn hard. This also leads into my second issue: portals. They make the enemies pretty much nothing more than a minor inconvenience, and they are pretty easy to open up if you do it within the first minute or 2. The solution here is much easier than the first problem, and it's to make portals teleport you to a specific portal on the map rather than you pick it. Now granted, I don't do game design so I have 0 clue how well this would work or if people like it, but I feel like it might be a bit better than js running to a portal to tp to cardmaster. TL;DR: Feed The Pit is one of the best games currently on the steam store, and at this price with all the content you get from this game(not including the 2 free updates in the works), there is no reason somebody shouldn't atleast give the game a try. Everything from the characters to the world to the pit is done so incredibly well and I am so excited to see what Act 2 and 3 have in store. And as always my dear cultists, FEED. THE. PIT.

What an absolutely phenomenal game. I found the developers and Feed The Pit through AstralSpiff's Deadseat videos, and after watching them, I was determined to experience whatever game the Devs made next for myself. Boy am I glad I did, now I can play it AND watch Spiffs video! Seriously, this is an absolutely remarkable game, every inch of it oozes with detail and thought and care. An engaging and re-playable game loop, incredibly designed creatures with fun mechanics which wrap back into the narrative, wonderful characterization which is accurate to how real cults function and that makes me care for every character, creative and gorgeous map design, and an incredibly intriguing story to boot. All of this in just Act One! A challenge mode and the 2nd and 3rd Acts should be releasing in the coming months, so if you're on the fence about buying, just do it. Its so worth it. Thanks to the devs and testers and everyone else who made / contributed to this game, all of you are awesome

This game's first act was a well thought out experience that surprisingly never wavered once. The gameplay loop is unique, fun, and engaging. It is familiar to me and I enjoyed the "Hide and Seek" aspect of the map and cards. The monster were cool and pretty scary, albeit not the most unique. I did not spend much time with the Flesh Thief, but the other two monsters in the game (the Spriggan and Little Rabbit) were frightening to say the least -- especially the Spriggan. However the thing I enjoyed the most out of this game was the story, The dialogue was fun and engaging, it felt human and each character has their own quirk which I liked too. The gameplay loop accompanied by the overarching mystery with minigames sprinkled in between missions can't help but remind me of Five Nights at Freddy's so I am very very excited to see where the rest of the story goes! Great game, worth the buy, and doing so directly supports funding to the next two acts (as stated by the devs in their most recent dev log) so pick it up! Solid 9.1/10!!
